alpha_refinement_sweep_2026_05_11.purpose: Tighter alpha grid (0.42 / 0.43 / 0.44) between 0.40 and 0.45 to test whether a sweet spot exists that brings 8px external back inside the 7% alternate tolerance while preserving R40 microscopy capacity.

trade_off_pattern_observation.alpha_0p42: 8 px −17.44% (large gain), 0.8 px +7.81%, 0.08 px +11.29% — trades small-scale stability for large-scale gain
trade_off_pattern_observation.alpha_0p43: 8 px −5.91%, 0.8 px −3.15%, 0.08 px +21.52% — improves two scales but 0.08 px takes the hit
trade_off_pattern_observation.alpha_0p45_existing: 8 px +22.80% (loss), 0.8 px +1.33%, 0.08 px −2.85% — opposite pattern from 0.42/0.43; trades large-scale for small-scale stability

alpha_refinement_sweep_2026_05_11.interpretation: Tighter alpha grid did NOT find a sweet spot that fits all three external scales within 7% tolerance.  However the sweep revealed a non-linear structure: weight averaging at different alphas produces distinct trade-off patterns rather than a smooth interpolation.  Linear extrapolation from α=0.45 (×1.257 local→external ratio) predicted α=0.43 external 8 px ≈ 0.188 / +21.6%; actual was 0.145 / −5.91%, off by a wide margin.  This suggests R40 weight averaging has multiple local optima across the alpha axis — α=0.43 and α=0.45 sit in opposite trade-off subspaces.  All three alphas remain RESEARCH_CAPACITY_ONLY, but the new evidence reshapes the picture of R40's failure mode: it is not simply 'R40 weight averaging cannot pass external GMF', it is 'no single alpha point fits all three scales simultaneously'.
alpha_refinement_sweep_2026_05_11.next_step_hint_only: Combining α=0.43-style 8 px / 0.8 px improvement with a030-style 0.08 px improvement (a030 is +6.42% on 0.8 px but −15.97% on 0.08 px) could theoretically cover all three scales; experimentally untested.  Not a recommendation, just an observation that the two side tracks now occupy complementary trade-off subspaces.

internal_external_divergence.root_cause: Circle-fit noise floor dominates internal step_std once real step variance drops below ~0.15 px.

alpha_linear_extrapolation_caveat.context: Triggered by R40 alpha refinement sweep (alpha_refinement_sweep_2026_05_11 under R40_a045).
alpha_linear_extrapolation_caveat.observation: Linear extrapolation from a single (alpha, external) pair to a neighbouring alpha is unreliable. Predicted vs actual on R40 alpha sweep: predicted alpha=0.43 external 8 px ≈ 0.188 (+21.6% vs COMBO) using the ×1.257 local→external ratio from alpha=0.45; actual alpha=0.43 external 8 px = 0.1454 (−5.91% vs COMBO). Direction reversed.
alpha_linear_extrapolation_caveat.explanation: Weight averaging at different alpha values can land in distinct trade-off subspaces rather than smoothly interpolating. Three R40 alphas (0.42 / 0.43 / 0.45) showed three different external Δ patterns: alpha=0.42 trades 0.8 px and 0.08 px for large 8 px gain; alpha=0.43 improves both 8 px and 0.8 px but hurts 0.08 px; alpha=0.45 improves 0.08 px but hurts 8 px.  No monotonic alpha→external relationship was observed.
alpha_linear_extrapolation_caveat.guidance: Do not extrapolate external GMF outcomes from local ring guard numbers, or from a single neighbouring alpha, when local step_std is near the circle-fit noise floor (~0.15 px). Run the external GMF measurement on the actual checkpoint before drawing trade-off conclusions.

R39 closing finding (2026-05-03, synthetic microscopy demo): on synthetic content outside the R39 training distribution (IC chip + bright grid + textured surface + edge defects), both a030 and COMBO show a hard capability ceiling — grid pattern is erased, texture is filtered away as noise, IC edges have ringing. Lighter input noise (alpha=160 vs 100) does not improve reconstruction, ruling out noise as the bottleneck. The limit is set by R39 training stages 1-9 only covering 'clean geometric primitives on neutral-gray background'. a030's promotion case within its actual scope (ring + simple shapes) is unaffected, but a030 should not be treated as a general microscopy reconstruction model. This finding became the R40 training-data coverage round (periodic structures, texture surfaces, large bright IC-style regions, irregular edge defects) — still controlled synthetic, no real-machine images in training. Details in Experiments/R39_ShapeGeneralization/reports/R39_RESULTS.md section 'Synthetic Microscopy Demo'.
